theme: The founder's most visible ask (stunning editors) alongside the four residual gate holes that fresh-context reviews proved real. Every one of the four is a gate that catches its named defect and misses a variant — recorded, not guessed.

sharedRules.note: Four other agents work this same checkout. Write only your declared files. Never run git. Never run npm run build, test:ui, meadow proof, or npm install. Run npx tsc --noEmit and your own spec by path.

ED01.founderWords: 'make the editors stunning'. The builder is the product's centre of gravity and where a judge spends the most time. It reads as capable rather than considered.
context: THIS IS A CRAFT NODE. No new capability, no new component, no new dependency. The design system already exists and is good — a token ladder (--tone-* raw triplets wrapped by --aura-*/--st-*), three named motion durations in a 150-250ms band with one damped house curve, a single focus ring, and a spacing scale on a 1.5 ratio. The job is to USE it properly in the builder.

READ FIRST: docs/BRAND-VOICE-GUIDE.md before touching a word, and the token block at the top of globals.css before touching a colour. If you find yourself typing a hex literal, stop — that is the signal you are working outside the system rather than in it.

STUNNING HERE MEANS CALMER, NOT LOUDER. This brand's own guardrails ban Apple-fragment cosplay, superlatives, and decoration carrying no information. Hierarchy, spacing, restraint and type doing the work. A page that is easier to read IS the deliverable.

AX01 just built a keyboard path through these exact controls — arrow-key vertex movement, numeric fields, a named object list, one aria-live region. Run tests/graph-keyboard.spec.ts before you finish. Breaking it to make something prettier is the worst possible trade.
writeSet: app/app/globals.css (.builder-* selectors only — NOT the token blocks, NOT .margin-*, NOT .zoning-*)
rejectionGates: NOT ONE NEW HEX LITERAL. Every colour from the token ladder. css-tokens.spec.ts catches an undefined variable; nothing catches a hardcoded colour except you and the spec you write.
NOT ONE NEW HAND-TUNED DURATION. interface-motion.spec.ts already fails the build on a literal duration in an app-surface transition.
prefers-reduced-motion must still still everything from the tokens, with no per-rule opt-in.
THE FOCUS RING IS DECIDED: one solid outline from --focus-ring-*, and it never glows. Do not restyle it.

MEASURE, DO NOT ASSERT, ANY HIERARCHY CLAIM YOU MAKE. A sibling node in the last wave wrote 'the unanswered count is the largest type' in a CSS comment and it was false on every phone, because a clamp resolved to its floor. If you claim one thing outranks another, assert it with computed font sizes at 390, 768 and 1280 — the claim in the comment is worth nothing.

EX06.job: Close the structural hole in the PDF completeness assertion — the one the review called wider than the gap the node itself disclosed.
EX06.theFinding: `paintedPaths` reduces every path to an UNORDERED BAG of points and `markPlacementProblems` compares only (first point, bounding box). Order, point count, connectivity and the paint operator are all invisible. Proven by injection: permuting two vertices of every path turns the A3 floor-plan wall poche into a bowtie and all 17 tests stay green. Three more misses were demonstrated the same way.
rejectionGates: THE ASSERTION MUST FAIL ON A VERTEX PERMUTATION. Build the bowtie, watch it go red, restore, paste the failure text. A drawing set whose walls can render as bowties and pass is not a drawing set.
Order and point count must enter the comparison — a bag of points is not a path. Keep the bounding-box and first-point checks alongside; they are real properties, just insufficient.
Do not weaken any existing assertion to make room.

TR02.job: Finish the truth gate: guard deployment and token STATUS prose, not just numbers.
TR02.theFinding: TR01 closed the spec-count and plan-count half. The half that motivated it is still open: docs/DEPLOYMENTS.md read 'Aura remains testnet-only ... no HOMES token' a full day after the token went live, and nothing would catch that recurring. release-truth.spec.ts pins WORDING and never reads DEPLOYMENTS.md at all.
rejectionGates: EVERY EXPECTED VALUE DERIVES FROM CODE. Assert documents against the constants in lib/homes/token.ts and the status in lib/homes/fund.ts — never against a second hand-typed constant in the spec, which would only prove two people typed the same thing.

PROVE IT ON THE HISTORICAL DEFECT. Temporarily restore the old 'Aura remains testnet-only' wording to DEPLOYMENTS.md, watch the gate go red, restore, and paste what you saw. A truth gate that would not have caught the drift that motivated it is decoration.
NO NETWORK. The suite runs offline and the site is a static export. The on-chain facts live in lib/homes/token.ts as constants; assert documents against those.
Do not weaken release-truth's existing wording pins — they caught real banned-phrase regressions. Add, do not replace.

FURN03.job: Close the AWG-spout breach and the methodological flaw behind it.
FURN03.theFinding: The per-part morph rule catches the vanity counterexample but misses the AWG spout (fixtures.ts:3173) — which sits under the source's own comment 'Louvre and spout are CONSTANT', the identical authorial pattern to the vanity's. AND the review named a flaw worth more than the breach: the threshold analysis established margin by measuring honest parts that CHANGE and showing each clears a bound. It never measured honest parts that are CONSTANT, which is the population the rule actually governs.
rejectionGates: REDO THE THRESHOLD ANALYSIS OVER THE RIGHT POPULATION — the constant parts. Report the separation you measure. If the thresholds cannot separate honest constants from breaches, say so plainly and pin the weaker property rather than shipping a number that looks measured and is not.
THE AWG SPOUT BREACH MUST GO RED. Build it, watch it fail, restore, paste the text.
Do not weaken the vanity counterexample that already works.

MK03.job: Make the round-trip gate see nested loss.
MK03.theFinding: The `lost`/`survived` check runs against the top-level key list only; nested losslessness rests entirely on a toEqual that a sub-object comparison can satisfy. Demonstrated by adding a field the converter does not know.
rejectionGates: THE GATE MUST FAIL ON A NESTED UNKNOWN FIELD. Build it, watch it go red, restore, paste the text.

Rejecting unknown keys should be recursive, and the refusal should name the PATH to the offending key, not just its name — a contributor told 'unknown key' about a field three levels down learns nothing.
